label: Where automation plugs in: APIs, CI testing, ticketing and escalation

mentor.diagnosis: You treated automation as one capability rather than as a set of integration points. The exam asks which point in the workflow the automation sits at.
contrast: Systems acting on each other without a human relaying
The plumbing everything else depends on
Security checks running on every commit and build
Flaws found while they are cheap, before release
Raising a tracked work item from an alert or a finding
Nothing is lost between detection and someone owning it
Routing onward automatically when nobody responds in time
Removes the single point of failure of one unavailable person
Provisioning and revoking as roles change or incidents require
Revocation that happens in seconds rather than at someone's convenience
mentor.rule: Ticket creation records that something needs doing. Escalation handles nobody doing it. They are adjacent and separately named, and the exam tests the difference.
mentor.tell: An alert that generated no follow-up points to ticket creation. An alert that sat unactioned for a weekend points to escalation.
mentor.trap: Automating ticket creation on a noisy alert source multiplies the noise into a backlog. Tuning has to come first, or automation industrialises the problem.
